claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2A comparing control and Dot1l KD BAT cells.

claims.claim: Dot1l KD BAT cells had decreased oxygen consumption rate (OCR) in oligomycin-, FCCP-, and rotenone/antimycin A-treated conditions.
claims.source: Moreover, Dot1l KD BAT cells had decreased oxygen consumption rate (OCR) in oligomycin-, FCCP-, and rotenone/antimycin A-treated conditions (Figure 2B, left).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by Seahorse OCR measurement data shown in Figure 2B comparing control and Dot1l KD BAT cells.

claims.claim: The uncoupled respiration of Dot1l KD cells was significantly lower than the control BAT cells in both basal and in forskolin-stimulated conditions.
claims.source: Notably, the uncoupled respiration of Dot1l KD cells was significantly lower than the control BAT cells in both basal and in forskolin-stimulated conditions (Figure 2B, right).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by Seahorse OCR measurement data shown in Figure 2B comparing control and Dot1l KD BAT cells under different conditions.

claims.claim: Dot1l knockdown had no effect on adipogenic markers or lipid accumulation.
claims.source: Indeed, there was no difference in expression of adipogenic marks, such as Fabp4, Pparg, Adipoq and no difference in lipid accumulation detected by Oil Red O staining (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR and Oil Red O staining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A comparing control and Dot1l KD BAT cells.

claims.claim: Dot1l inhibition resulted in a significant reduction in mRNA and protein levels for Ucp1 by 90%.
claims.source: Dot1l inhibition resulted in a significant reduction in mRNA and protein levels for Ucp1 by 90% (Figure 2C), while not affecting Dot1l protein stability (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 2C comparing DMSO control and EPZ5676-treated BAT cells.

claims.claim: Expression of other BAT-enriched Zc3h10 target genes, such as Tfam, Nrf1, Cox7a, and Cox8b, was decreased by 40–80% upon Dot1l inhibition.
claims.source: Expression of other BAT-enriched Zc3h10 target genes, such as Tfam, Nrf1, Cox7a, and Cox8b, was decreased by 40–80%, whereas Pparg expression was not affected (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2C comparing DMSO control and EPZ5676-treated BAT cells.

claims.claim: EPZ5676 treated cells had significantly decreased H3K79me3 at −4.6 kb Ucp1 region as well as Tfam and Nrf1 promoter regions.
claims.source: EPZ5676 treated cells had significantly decreased H3K79me3 at −4.6 kb Ucp1 region as well as Tfam and Nrf1 promoter regions, while having no difference at the Gapdh promoter region as compared to the control cells (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 2D comparing DMSO control and EPZ5676-treated BAT cells overexpressing Dot1l.

claims.claim: Dot1l-M55L mutant significantly reduced occupancy of H3K79me3 at the promoter regions of Ucp1, Tfam and Nrf1, compared to WT-Dot1l.
claims.source: Dot1l-M55L mutant significantly reduced occupancy of H3K79me3 at the promoter regions of Ucp1, Tfam and Nrf1, compared to WT-Dot1l, while not affecting Gapdh promoter region (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C comparing WT-Dot1l and M55L-Dot1l mutant.

claims.claim: Dot1l overexpression significantly increased thermogenic gene expression including Ucp1, Cox8b, Cidea.
claims.source: As expected, Dot1l overexpression significantly increased thermogenic gene expression including Ucp1, Cox8b, Cidea, while Zc3h10 KD significantly decreased these genes (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2E comparing GFP control, Dot1l OE, Zc3h10 KD, and combined conditions.

claims.claim: Zc3h10 KD significantly decreased thermogenic gene expression.
claims.source: As expected, Dot1l overexpression significantly increased thermogenic gene expression including Ucp1, Cox8b, Cidea, while Zc3h10 KD significantly decreased these genes (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2E comparing GFP control, Dot1l OE, Zc3h10 KD, and combined conditions.

claims.claim: The population of ERthermAC+ cells in Dot1l OE cells was decreased by 10%, indicating increased thermogenesis.
claims.source: Upon forskolin treatment, the population of ERthermAC+ cells in Dot1l OE cells was decreased by 10%, which indicated that the cell population with higher temperature was increased by approximately 2.5-fold (Figure 2F, Left), calculated by the percent decrease from ERthermAC+ population in control cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 2F measuring ERthermAC fluorescence in Dot1l OE cells.

claims.claim: ERthermAC+ cells in Zc3h10 KD cells were significantly increased by 10%, indicating decreased heat production.
claims.source: In contrast, ERthermAC+ cells in Zc3h10 KD cells were significantly increased by 10%, indicating that Zc3h10 ablation decreased heat production in BAT cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 2F measuring ERthermAC fluorescence in Zc3h10 KD cells.

claims.claim: Zc3h10 KD in Dot1l overexpressing cells prevented Dot1l-induced thermogenesis.
claims.source: Moreover, Zc3h10 KD in Dot1l overexpressing cells showed low ERthermAC+ cells that were similar to control cells, indicating that Zc3h10 ablation prevented Dot1l-induced thermogenesis.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 2F measuring ERthermAC fluorescence in combined Dot1l OE and Zc3h10 KD cells.

claims.claim: Dot1l overexpression in Zc3h10 KD BAT cells had the uncoupled OCR comparable to that of Zc3h10 KD, which was significantly lower than the control cells.
claims.source: Furthermore, when we measured OCR by using Seahorse, Dot1l overexpression in Zc3h10 KD BAT cells had the uncoupled OCR comparable to that of Zc3h10 KD, which was significantly lower than the control cells (Figure 2F, Right).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by Seahorse OCR measurement data shown in Figure 2F comparing different conditions.

claims.claim: Dot1l KO pool had significantly decreased Ucp1, Dio2, Elov3, Cox8b, and Nrf1 mRNA levels by more than 50% compared to the control BAT cells.
claims.source: We found that Dot1l KO pool had significantly decreased Ucp1, Dio2, Elov3, Cox8b, and Nrf1 mRNA levels by more than 50% compared to the control BAT cells, while Zc3h10 overexpression increased thermogenic gene expression as expected (Figure 2G).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2G comparing control and Dot1l KO pool.

claims.claim: Zc3h10 overexpression in Dot1l KO pool did not rescue the decreased BAT-gene expression.
claims.source: Importantly, Zc3h10 overexpression in Dot1l KO pool did not rescue the decreased BAT- gene expression, remaining in significantly reduced thermogenic gene expression, an evidence that Dot1l is critical for Zc3h10-induced thermogenic gene program.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2G comparing Zc3h10 OE in control versus Dot1l KO pool.

claims.claim: Zc3h10 OE significantly reduced ERthermAC+ population compared to control.
claims.source: Zc3h10 OE significantly reduced ERthermAC+ population in compared to control; while two independent Dot1l KO pools had increased ERthermAC+ population, indicating decreased thermogenesis (Figure 2H).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 2H measuring ERthermAC fluorescence.

claims.claim: Dot1l KO pools had increased ERthermAC+ population, indicating decreased thermogenesis.
claims.source: Zc3h10 OE significantly reduced ERthermAC+ population in compared to control; while two independent Dot1l KO pools had increased ERthermAC+ population, indicating decreased thermogenesis (Figure 2H).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 2H measuring ERthermAC fluorescence.

claims.claim: Zc3h10 OE did not affect ERthermAC+ population in Dot1l KO pools.
claims.source: Notably, Zc3h10 OE did not affect ERthermAC+ population in Dot1l KO pools.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data comparing Zc3h10 OE effects in control versus Dot1l KO pools.

claims.claim: Dot1l overexpression alone increased Ucp1 mRNA levels over two-fold in 3T3-L1 cells.
claims.source: Interestingly, Dot1l overexpression alone increased Ucp1 mRNA levels over two-fold, probably due to the presence of endogenous Dot1l in 3T3-L1 cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data measuring Ucp1 expression in 3T3-L1 cells with Dot1l overexpression.

claims.claim: Co-overexpression of both Dot1l and Zc3h10 resulted in a further increase in Ucp1 mRNA levels by three-fold and Ucp1 protein levels in 3T3-L1 cells.
claims.source: Co-overexpression of both Dot1l and Zc3h10 resulted in a further increase in Ucp1 mRNA levels by three-fold and Ucp1 protein levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and E comparing different overexpression conditions in 3T3-L1 cells.

claims.claim: Co-overexpression of both Dot1l and Zc3h10 further increased the total OCR as well as uncoupled OCR in 3T3-L1 cells.
claims.source: Co-overexpression of both Dot1l and Zc3h10 further increased the total OCR as well as uncoupled OCR, suggesting cooperative function of Dot1l and Zc3h10 in browning of 3T3-L1 cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by Seahorse OCR measurement data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F comparing different overexpression conditions in 3T3-L1 cells.

claims.claim: BAT from EPZ5676 treated mice showed significantly decreased mRNA levels for Ucp1, Nrf1, and Tfam, as well as other thermogenic genes, such as Ppargc1a and Elovl3.
claims.source: Indeed, BAT from the inhibitor treated mice showed significantly decreased mRNA levels for Ucp1, Nrf1, and Tfam, as well as other thermogenic genes, such as Ppargc1a and Elovl3, while no changes in adipogenic transcription factor, such as Pparg (Figure 3B, middle).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3B comparing saline control and EPZ5676-treated mice.

claims.claim: Immunoblotting detected significantly lower Ucp1 protein levels in BAT of EPZ5676 treated mice compared to the control mice.
claims.source: Also, the immunoblotting detected significantly lower Ucp1 protein levels in BAT of EPZ5676 treated mice compared to the control mice (Figure 3B, middle).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3B comparing saline control and EPZ5676-treated mice.

claims.claim: EPZ5676 treatment decreased thermogenic gene expression in iWAT.
claims.source: Similarly, EPZ5676 treatment also decreased thermogenic gene expression in iWAT, WAT depot known to undergo browning (Figure 3B, right), but not in pWAT or in liver (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3B comparing saline control and EPZ5676-treated mice in iWAT.

claims.claim: EPZ5676 treatment did not affect thermogenic gene expression in pWAT or in liver.
claims.source: Similarly, EPZ5676 treatment also decreased thermogenic gene expression in iWAT, WAT depot known to undergo browning (Figure 3B, right), but not in pWAT or in liver (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A comparing saline control and EPZ5676-treated mice in pWAT and liver.

claims.claim: After 4 hr of cold exposure, the body temperature of the EPZ5676-treated mice was 4°C lower compared to their non-treated littermates.
claims.source: After 4 hr of cold exposure, the body temperature of the EPZ5676-treated mice was 4°C lower compared to their non-treated littermates, demonstrating the significantly reduced thermogenic capacity (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by rectal temperature measurement data shown in Figure 3C comparing saline control and EPZ5676-treated mice during cold exposure.

claims.claim: EPZ5676 treated mice had significantly lower VO2 than the control mice at 4°C.
claims.source: Indeed, EPZ5676 treated mice had significantly lower VO2 than the control mice at 4°C (Figure 3D), whereas food intake and locomotive activity were similar between the two groups (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by indirect calorimetry data shown in Figure 3D comparing saline control and EPZ5676-treated mice.

claims.claim: Food intake and locomotive activity were similar between control and EPZ5676-treated mice.
claims.source: Indeed, EPZ5676 treated mice had significantly lower VO2 than the control mice at 4°C (Figure 3D), whereas food intake and locomotive activity were similar between the two groups (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by food intake and locomotor activity measurement data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B comparing saline control and EPZ5676-treated mice.

claims.claim: Dot1l-BKO mice had a 70% reduction in Dot1l mRNA and protein levels in BAT.
claims.source: Dot1l-BKO mice had a 70% reduction in Dot1l mRNA and protein levels in BAT.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR and immunoblotting data comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claims.claim: Dot1l-BKO mice showed a 60% decrease in Dot1l mRNA level in iWAT.
claims.source: Dot1l-BKO mice also showed a 60% decrease in Dot1l mRNA level in iWAT, probably due to the mild cold exposure at room temperature that can induce Ucp1+ adipocytes in iWAT (Figure 4A, right).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice, with speculation about the mechanism.

claims.claim: Ucp1 expression was significantly reduced by 40% and 60% in BAT and iWAT, respectively, in Dot1l-BKO mice.
claims.source: Importantly, Ucp1 expression was significantly reduced by 40% and 60% in BAT and iWAT, respectively (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4B comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claims.claim: Ucp1 protein level was reduced significantly in BAT of Dot1l-BKO mice.
claims.source: Ucp1 protein level also was reduced significantly, as detect in BAT (Figure 4B right).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4B comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claims.claim: Expression of other BAT enriched genes, such as Dio2 and Cidea, and other Zc3h10 target genes, such as Tfam and Nrf1, were all significantly decreased in BAT and iWAT of Dot1l-BKO mice.
claims.source: In addition, expression of other BAT enriched genes, such as Dio2 and Cidea, and other Zc3h10 target genes, such as Tfam and Nrf1, were all significantly decreased in BAT and iWAT of Dot1l-BKO mice, compared to WT littermates (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4C comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claims.claim: A 50% reduction in di-methylation and a 70% reduction in tri-methylation of H3K79 at the −4.6 kb Ucp1 promoter region was detected in Dot1l-BKO mice.
claims.source: Indeed, we detected a 50% reduction in di-methylation and a 70% reduction in tri-methylation of H3K79 at the −4.6 kb Ucp1 promoter region (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4D comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claims.claim: H3K79 methylation status at the −200 bp Nrf1 promoter region and at the +50 bp Tfam region was decreased in Dot1l-BKO mice.
claims.source: Similar to the −4.6 kb Ucp1 promoter region, H3K79 methylation status at the −200 bp Nrf1 promoter region and at the +50 bp Tfam region was also decreased (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4D comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claims.claim: After 3 hr of cold exposure, the body temperature of Dot1l-BKO mice was 5°C lower than that of control mice.
claims.source: After 3 hr of cold exposure, the body temperature of Dot1l-BKO mice was 5°C lower than that of control mice (Figure 4E), an in vivo evidence of the requirement of Dot1l for cold-induced thermogenesis.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by rectal temperature measurement data shown in Figure 4E comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice during cold exposure.

claims.claim: The Dot1l-BKO mice had significantly reduced VO2 compared to WT littermates at room temperature and at 4°C in particular.
claims.source: Indeed, the Dot1l-BKO mice had significantly reduced VO2 compared to WT littermates at room temperature and at 4°C in particular, while locomotor activity and food consumption were similar (Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by indirect calorimetry data shown in Figure 4F comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claims.claim: OCR in BAT from Dot1l-BKO mice was decreased by 20%.
claims.source: We found OCR in BAT from Dot1l-BKO mice to be decreased by 20%. (Figure 4F, right).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by Seahorse OCR measurement data shown in Figure 4F comparing BAT from Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claims.claim: By 13 weeks, the Dot1l-BKO mice were approximately 8 g heavier relative to the control mice.
claims.source: By 13 weeks, the Dot1l-BKO mice were approximately 8 g heavier relative to the control mice (Figure 4G), and the Dot1l-BKO had significantly larger iWAT and pWAT depots, which primarily accounted for the higher total body weights of Dot1l-BKO mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by body weight measurement data shown in Figure 4G comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice on HFD.

claims.claim: The Dot1l-BKO had significantly larger iWAT and pWAT depots, which primarily accounted for the higher total body weights of Dot1l-BKO mice.
claims.source: By 13 weeks, the Dot1l-BKO mice were approximately 8 g heavier relative to the control mice (Figure 4G), and the Dot1l-BKO had significantly larger iWAT and pWAT depots, which primarily accounted for the higher total body weights of Dot1l-BKO mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by tissue mass measurement data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claims.claim: Blood glucose levels of Dot1l-BKO mice on HFD were significantly higher during the course of glucose tolerance test (GTT).
claims.source: In addition, blood glucose levels of Dot1l-BKO mice on HFD were significantly higher during the course of glucose tolerance test (GTT) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, Left), and they had significantly impaired insulin sensitivity when subjected to an insulin tolerance test (ITT) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, Right).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by GTT data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice on HFD.

claims.claim: Dot1l-BKO mice had significantly impaired insulin sensitivity when subjected to an insulin tolerance test (ITT).
claims.source: In addition, blood glucose levels of Dot1l-BKO mice on HFD were significantly higher during the course of glucose tolerance test (GTT) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, Left), and they had significantly impaired insulin sensitivity when subjected to an insulin tolerance test (ITT) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, Right).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by ITT data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C comparing Dot1l f/f control and Dot1l-BKO mice on HFD.

claims.claim: Zc3h10 overexpressing mice by injection had increased expression of BAT-enriched genes, such as Ucp1, Cox8b, and Cidea, compared to the control mice.
claims.source: As we previously have reported that overexpression of Zc3h10 in adipose tissue enhances thermogenic gene expression (Yi et al., 2019), Zc3h10 overexpressing mice by injection had increased expression of BAT-enriched genes, such as Ucp1, Cox8b, and Cidea, compared to the control mice.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data comparing GFP control and Zc3h10 OE mice, with citation to Yi et al., 2019 for previous findings.

claims.claim: Expression of BAT-enriched genes remained significantly reduced in Dot1l-BKO even upon Zc3h10 overexpression.
claims.source: More importantly, expression BAT-enriched genes remained significantly reduced in Dot1l-BKO even upon Zc3h10 overexpression, while adipogenic markers, such as Pparg, remained unchanged (Figure 4H).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4H comparing WT+GFP, WT+Zc3h10 OE, and Dot1l-BKO+Zc3h10 OE mice.

claims.claim: Zc3h10 OE mice had higher core body temperature compared to the control mice after 4 hr of cold exposure.
claims.source: Moreover, when these mice were subjected to cold exposure, Zc3h10 OE mice had higher core body temperature compared to the control mice after 4 hr (Figure 5I).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by rectal temperature measurement data shown in Figure 4I (note: text says Figure 5I but this appears to be Figure 4I based on context) comparing control and Zc3h10 OE mice during cold exposure.

claims.claim: Dot1l-BKO Zc3h10 OE mice were severely cold sensitive as their body temperature was significantly lower than the control and Zc3h10 OE mice.
claims.source: However, Dot1l-BKO Zc3h10 OE mice were severely cold sensitive as their body temperature was significantly lower than the control and Zc3h10 OE mice.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by rectal temperature measurement data comparing control, Zc3h10 OE, and Dot1l-BKO Zc3h10 OE mice during cold exposure.

claims.claim: Dot1l-BKO mice had significantly reduced peaks near the transcription start sites (TSS) in ATAC-seq analysis.
claims.source: We detected a high number of peaks in the aggregate plot (upper) and high ATAC-seq read distributions concentrated at the TSS in the heatmap for the WT (lower), while Dot1l-BKO had significantly reduced peaks near the transcription start sites (TSS), signifying reduced open chromatin regions, as H3K79 methylation has been reported as an activation marker. (Figure 5A, left).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5A comparing WT and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claims.claim: The most affected pathways by Dot1l ablation in BAT were cell cycle, chromatin organization, mitochondrion organization, thermogenesis.
claims.source: The most affected pathways were cell cycle, chromatin organization, mitochondrion organization, thermogenesis etc (Figure 5A, middle).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis of ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5A comparing WT and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claims.claim: Dot1l-BKO mice had much smaller peaks around promoters of Ucp1, Cox8b, and Cox7a compared to WT mice.
claims.source: Dot1l-BKO mice had much smaller peaks around promoters of Ucp1, Cox8b, and Cox7a compared to WT mice (Figure 5A, right), consistent with significantly decreased thermogenic gene expression in the Dot1l-BKO mice (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by ATAC-seq peak visualization data shown in Figure 5A comparing WT and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claims.claim: Gene ontology of genes that were at least two-fold downregulated in Dot1l-BKO mice revealed that mitochondrion organization, oxidative phosphorylation and cold-induced thermogenesis were some of the most affected processes.
claims.source: Gene ontology of genes that were at least two-fold downregulated in Dot1l-BKO mice revealed that mitochondrion organization, oxidative phosphorylation and cold-induced thermogenesis were some of the most affected processes (Figure 5B, right).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis of RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B comparing WT and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claims.claim: The downregulated thermogenic genes in Dot1l-BKO mice include Ucp1, Cox8b, Elovl3, and Ppargc1a.
claims.source: Notably, the downregulated thermogenic genes include Ucp1, Cox8b, Elovl3, and Ppargc1a as well as those related to mitochondrion organization and oxidative phosphorylation such as Nrf1, Cox20, Tomm13, and Immp21 (Figure 5B, left).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq heatmap data shown in Figure 5B comparing WT and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claims.claim: Dot1l-BKO had decreased expression of Aifm2, a recently reported BAT-specific enzyme that converts NADH to NAD to sustain robust glycolysis to fuel thermogenesis.
claims.source: Also, we found Dot1l-BKO had decreased expression of Aifm2, a recently reported BAT-specific enzyme that converts NADH to NAD to sustain robust glycolysis to fuel thermogenesis (Nguyen et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data with citation to Nguyen et al., 2020 for the function of Aifm2.

claims.claim: Upregulated genes in Dot1l-BKO mice involved in chromatin compaction and gene repression include Hdac3, Hdac4, and Dnmt1.
claims.source: In fact, we detected upregulated genes involved in chromatin compaction and gene repression, such as Hdac3, Hdac4, and Dnmt1, further supporting that Dot1l increases chromatin accessibility (Figure 5B, right).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B comparing WT and Dot1l-BKO mice.

claims.claim: About 82% of the total of downregulated genes in RNA-seq were also detected from the ATAC-seq dataset.
claims.source: We then compared RNA-seq data to ATAC-seq obtained to identify common downregulated pathways found at lower levels using ATACs upon Dot1l ablation in Ucp1+ cells, and we found about 82% of the total of downregulated genes were also detected from the ATAC-seq dataset (Figure 5C, left).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 5C comparing RNA-seq and ATAC-seq datasets.

claims.claim: Similar processes between RNA-seq and ATAC-seq datasets include regulation of cold-induced thermogenesis, mitochondrial transcription and membrane organization, oxidative phosphorylation, and lipid catabolic process.
claims.source: Some of similar processes between the two datasets include regulation of cold-induced thermogenesis, mitochondrial transcription and membrane organization, oxidative phosphorylation, and lipid catabolic process, (Figure 5C, right).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis of shared genes shown in Figure 5C comparing RNA-seq and ATAC-seq datasets.

claims.claim: The cluster of shared genes between RNA-seq and ATAC-seq included thermogenic genes, such as Ucp1, Ppargc1a, Cox8b, Nrf1, and Cidea.
claims.source: Remarkably, the cluster of shared genes included thermogenic genes, such as Ucp1, Ppargc1a, Cox8b, Nrf1, and Cidea, further underscoring the importance of Dot1l in brown adipose tissue.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of shared genes between RNA-seq and ATAC-seq datasets.

claims.claim: Brown adipose tissue is a metabolically beneficial organ capable of dissipating chemical energy into heat, thereby increasing energy expenditure.
claims.source: Brown adipose tissue is a metabolically beneficial organ capable of dissipating chemical energy into heat, thereby increasing energy expenditure.
claims.evidence: This is a general statement about BAT function presented in the abstract.

claims.claim: Dot1l ablation in mice using Ucp1-Cre prevents activation of Ucp1 and other target genes to reduce thermogenic capacity and energy expenditure, promoting adiposity.
claims.source: Furthermore, we demonstrate that Dot1l ablation in mice using Ucp1-Cre prevents activation of Ucp1 and other target genes to reduce thermogenic capacity and energy expenditure, promoting adiposity.
claims.evidence: This claim summarizes findings from multiple experiments including gene expression, cold tolerance, oxygen consumption, and body weight measurements in Dot1l-BKO mice.

claims.claim: White adipose tissue (WAT) stores excess calories.
claims.source: Adipose tissue has a central role in controlling mammalian energy metabolism in that, while white adipose tissue (WAT) is to store excess calories, brown adipose tissue (BAT) is to dissipate energy via non-shivering thermogenesis (Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004.

claims.claim: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) dissipates energy via non-shivering thermogenesis.
claims.source: Adipose tissue has a central role in controlling mammalian energy metabolism in that, while white adipose tissue (WAT) is to store excess calories, brown adipose tissue (BAT) is to dissipate energy via non-shivering thermogenesis (Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004.

claims.claim: Classic brown adipocytes contain a high density of mitochondria that contain Uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1).
claims.source: Classic brown adipocytes contain a high density of mitochondria that contain Uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1), which uncouples respiration from ATP synthesis and generates heat instead (Farmer, 2008; Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Farmer, 2008 and Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004.

claims.claim: Ucp1 uncouples respiration from ATP synthesis and generates heat instead.
claims.source: Classic brown adipocytes contain a high density of mitochondria that contain Uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1), which uncouples respiration from ATP synthesis and generates heat instead (Farmer, 2008; Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Farmer, 2008 and Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004.

claims.claim: Beige/brite adipocytes in WAT depot are recruited upon cold exposure or β3-adrenergic stimulation.
claims.source: In addition, beige/brite adipocytes in WAT depot are recruited upon cold exposure or β3-adrenergic stimulation (Seale et al., 2008; Wang and Seale, 2016; Sanchez-Gurmaches et al., 2016; Cypess et al., 2009; Lichtenbelt et al., 2009; Virtanen et al., 2009; Chondronikola et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple references (Seale et al., 2008; Wang and Seale, 2016; Sanchez-Gurmaches et al., 2016; Cypess et al., 2009; Lichtenbelt et al., 2009; Virtanen et al., 2009; Chondronikola et al., 2014).

claims.claim: Adult human brown fat or brown fat-like tissue is inversely correlated with body mass index and visceral fat.

results.result: Dot1l is the only known H3K79 methyltransferase that catalyzes sequential mono-, di-, and tri-methylation of H3K79, which is located at the globular domain of nucleosomes. Dot1l lacks a SET domain but contains an AdoMET motif and is known to play roles in telomere silencing, cell cycle regulation, and MLL-related leukemogenesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C5 are well-supported by multiple citations to established literature (Min et al., 2003; van Leeuwen et al., 2002; Frederiks et al., 2008; Feng et al., 2002; Schulze et al., 2009; Okada et al., 2005; Nguyen and Zhang, 2011; Ng et al., 2002). These are established facts about Dot1l from prior work that provide necessary background context for the current study.

results.result: Dot1l directly interacts with Zc3h10 through its middle fragment (aa 501-1000) containing coiled coil motifs. This interaction was demonstrated in both overexpression systems and with endogenous proteins in BAT, and is not modulated by cold exposure.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C10 are strongly supported by multiple complementary experimental approaches including Co-IP with tagged proteins (C6), Co-IP with endogenous proteins (C7), GST pull-down assays demonstrating direct binding (C9), and domain mapping experiments (C10). The data shown in Figure 1A-C provide converging evidence for direct protein-protein interaction.

results.result: Dot1l is enriched in BAT compared to other tissues, enriched in the brown adipocyte fraction compared to SVF, induced upon cold exposure, and increased during BAT cell differentiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C11-C14 are supported by RT-qPCR and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1D-F. The expression pattern of Dot1l mirrors that of Zc3h10 and other thermogenic genes, supporting its potential role in thermogenesis. The data are internally consistent and use appropriate controls.

results.result: Dot1l synergistically activates the Ucp1 promoter with Zc3h10 (11-fold increase), while neither protein alone produces comparable activation. This synergistic activation requires Dot1l's catalytic activity, as demonstrated by the M55L mutant and EPZ5676 inhibitor experiments.
results.evaluation: Claims C15-C19 are well-supported by luciferase reporter assays shown in Figure 1G. The synergistic effect (11-fold vs 3-fold for Zc3h10 alone) is substantial and statistically significant. The requirement for catalytic activity is demonstrated through two independent approaches (M55L mutant and EPZ5676 inhibitor), strengthening the conclusion.

results.result: Dot1l and Zc3h10 co-occupy the same regions of the Ucp1 promoter (-4.6 kb) and Tfam promoter (+50 bp), as demonstrated by ChIP and Re-ChIP experiments.
results.evaluation: Claims C20-C21 are supported by ChIP-qPCR and Re-ChIP data shown in Figure 1H. The Re-ChIP experiment is particularly strong evidence for co-occupancy, as it demonstrates that both proteins are present on the same DNA molecules. The inclusion of a negative control (Gapdh promoter) strengthens the specificity of the findings.

results.result: Dot1l knockdown in BAT cells reduces Ucp1 and other thermogenic genes (Tfam, Nrf1, Elovl3) by ~50%, decreases oxygen consumption and uncoupled respiration, but does not affect adipogenic markers or lipid accumulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C22-C27 are supported by comprehensive data in Figure 2A-B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, including RT-qPCR, immunoblotting, Seahorse OCR measurements, and Oil Red O staining. The specificity for thermogenic genes without affecting adipogenesis (C27) is important for establishing that Dot1l's role is specific to thermogenesis rather than general adipocyte function.

results.result: Pharmacological inhibition of Dot1l with EPZ5676 reduces Ucp1 expression by 90% and other thermogenic genes by 40-80%, decreases H3K79me3 at thermogenic gene promoters, and this effect is recapitulated by the M55L catalytic mutant.
results.evaluation: Claims C28-C31 are strongly supported by data in Figure 2C-D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B-C. The use of both pharmacological inhibition and catalytic mutant provides orthogonal validation. The ChIP-qPCR data (C30, C31) mechanistically link the enzymatic activity to H3K79 methylation at specific target genes, with appropriate negative controls (Gapdh).

results.result: Dot1l overexpression increases thermogenic gene expression and thermogenesis (measured by ERthermAC and OCR), while Zc3h10 knockdown decreases these parameters. Importantly, Zc3h10 knockdown prevents Dot1l-induced thermogenesis, demonstrating that Dot1l requires Zc3h10 for its function.
results.evaluation: Claims C32-C37 are supported by comprehensive data in Figure 2E-F using RT-qPCR, immunoblotting, ERthermAC fluorescence, and Seahorse OCR measurements. The epistasis experiment (C36-C37) is particularly strong evidence that Dot1l functions downstream of or in cooperation with Zc3h10. The use of ERthermAC as a functional readout of thermogenesis is appropriate.

results.result: CRISPR-mediated Dot1l knockout reduces thermogenic gene expression by >50%, and Zc3h10 overexpression cannot rescue this defect. Dot1l KO increases ERthermAC+ population (indicating decreased thermogenesis), and Zc3h10 overexpression does not affect this phenotype in Dot1l KO cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C42 are supported by data in Figure 2G-H using CRISPR knockout pools. The failure of Zc3h10 overexpression to rescue Dot1l KO (C39, C42) provides strong genetic evidence that Dot1l is essential for Zc3h10 function. The use of two independent KO pools strengthens the conclusions. However, the incomplete knockout (~50% reduction) is a limitation.

results.result: In 3T3-L1 cells, Dot1l overexpression alone increases Ucp1 expression 2-fold, co-overexpression with Zc3h10 increases it 3-fold, and this correlates with increased total and uncoupled OCR.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C45 are supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D-F. The gain-of-function experiments in 3T3-L1 cells complement the loss-of-function studies in BAT cells. The speculation about endogenous Dot1l (C43) is reasonable but not directly tested. The functional validation with OCR measurements strengthens the conclusions.

results.result: In vivo EPZ5676 treatment decreases thermogenic gene expression in BAT and iWAT (but not pWAT or liver), reduces body temperature by 4°C during cold exposure, and decreases VO2 at 4°C without affecting food intake or locomotor activity.
results.evaluation: Claims C46-C52 are supported by comprehensive in vivo data in Figure 3B-D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B. The tissue specificity (C48-C49) is important for establishing that the effect is specific to thermogenic tissues. The lack of effect on food intake and activity (C52) rules out general sickness or behavioral changes. The 4°C temperature difference during cold exposure is physiologically significant.

results.result: Dot1l-BKO mice show 70% reduction in Dot1l in BAT and 60% in iWAT, with corresponding reductions in Ucp1 (40-60%) and other thermogenic genes (Dio2, Cidea, Tfam, Nrf1) at both mRNA and protein levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C57 are supported by RT-qPCR and immunoblotting data in Figure 4A-C. The incomplete knockout is acknowledged and explained by the Ucp1-Cre system. The coordinate downregulation of multiple thermogenic genes supports a broad role for Dot1l in the thermogenic program. The data are consistent across multiple genes and tissues.

results.result: Dot1l-BKO mice show 50% reduction in H3K79me2 and 70% reduction in H3K79me3 at the Ucp1 promoter (-4.6 kb), with similar reductions at Nrf1 and Tfam promoters.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C59 are supported by ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 4D. The mechanistic link between Dot1l loss and reduced H3K79 methylation at specific target genes is direct and expected. The data provide molecular evidence for how Dot1l regulates thermogenic gene expression. The specificity for Zc3h10 binding sites is notable.

results.result: Dot1l-BKO mice are severely cold intolerant (5°C lower body temperature after 3 hr at 4°C), have reduced VO2 at both room temperature and 4°C, and show 20% decreased OCR in isolated BAT.
results.evaluation: Claims C60-C62 are supported by physiological measurements in Figure 4E-F. The cold intolerance phenotype is severe and physiologically significant. The reduced VO2 and OCR provide mechanistic insight into the thermogenic defect. The consistency between whole-body and tissue-level measurements strengthens the conclusions.

results.result: Dot1l-BKO mice on HFD gain ~8 g more weight by 13 weeks, with significantly larger iWAT and pWAT depots, and show impaired glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C66 are supported by body weight, tissue mass, GTT, and ITT data in Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B-C. The metabolic phenotype is consistent with reduced thermogenic capacity. However, the causal relationship between reduced thermogenesis and increased adiposity/insulin resistance is correlative rather than directly demonstrated. The lack of food intake differences is important.

results.result: Zc3h10 overexpression in WT mice increases thermogenic gene expression and improves cold tolerance, but fails to rescue thermogenic gene expression or cold tolerance in Dot1l-BKO mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C70 are supported by in vivo rescue experiments in Figure 4H-I. The failure of Zc3h10 overexpression to rescue Dot1l-BKO provides strong genetic evidence that Dot1l is essential for Zc3h10 function in vivo. This complements the in vitro epistasis experiments and strengthens the model that Dot1l acts as a required coactivator for Zc3h10.

results.result: ATAC-seq analysis shows that Dot1l-BKO mice have significantly reduced chromatin accessibility near transcription start sites genome-wide, with the most affected pathways being cell cycle, chromatin organization, mitochondrion organization, and thermogenesis. Specific thermogenic genes (Ucp1, Cox8b, Cox7a) show much smaller ATAC-seq peaks in Dot1l-BKO mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C73 are supported by ATAC-seq data in Figure 5A. The genome-wide reduction in chromatin accessibility provides mechanistic insight into how Dot1l regulates gene expression. The pathway analysis is appropriate and the specific examples of thermogenic genes strengthen the conclusions. However, n=2 per group is a limitation for genome-wide studies.

results.result: RNA-seq analysis shows that genes downregulated >2-fold in Dot1l-BKO mice are enriched for mitochondrion organization, oxidative phosphorylation, and thermogenesis pathways, including Ucp1, Cox8b, Elovl3, Ppargc1a, Nrf1, and Aifm2. Upregulated genes include chromatin compaction factors (Hdac3, Hdac4, Dnmt1).
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C77 are supported by RNA-seq data in Figure 5B. The transcriptomic changes are consistent with the phenotypic observations and provide comprehensive molecular evidence for Dot1l's role in thermogenesis. The upregulation of chromatin compaction factors (C77) is particularly interesting and supports the model that Dot1l maintains open chromatin. However, n=2 pooled samples per group is a limitation.

results.result: Integration of ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data shows that 82% of downregulated genes in RNA-seq also show reduced chromatin accessibility in ATAC-seq, with shared pathways including cold-induced thermogenesis, mitochondrial organization, and oxidative phosphorylation. Shared genes include Ucp1, Ppargc1a, Cox8b, Nrf1, and Cidea.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C80 are supported by integrated analysis in Figure 5C. The high overlap (82%) between transcriptional changes and chromatin accessibility changes provides strong mechanistic evidence that Dot1l regulates thermogenic genes through chromatin remodeling. The identification of specific shared genes strengthens the biological interpretation.

results.result: Background information on brown adipose tissue function, beige adipocyte recruitment, human BAT correlations with obesity, and known transcriptional regulators of Ucp1.
results.evaluation: Claims C81, C83-C89 are well-supported by appropriate citations to established literature. These provide necessary background context for understanding the significance of the current work. The citations are appropriate and the statements accurately represent the cited work.

results.result: Background information on Zc3h10 as a BAT-enriched transcription factor that activates Ucp1 by binding to the -4.6 kb region, is phosphorylated by p38 MAPK, and whose manipulation affects thermogenic capacity and obesity.
results.evaluation: Claims C90-C94 are supported by citation to Yi et al., 2019, which is the authors' previous work. These claims provide essential background for understanding the current study's focus on Dot1l as a Zc3h10 interacting partner. The statements accurately represent the prior work.

results.result: Background information on H3K79 methylation as an activation mark, its role in enhancer-promoter interactions, correlation with other activation marks, and potential mechanisms involving inhibition of histone deacetylases.
results.evaluation: Claims C95-C100, C114, C116 are supported by appropriate citations to prior literature (Steger et al., 2008; Wood et al., 2018; Markenscoff-Papadimitriou et al., 2014; Gilan et al., 2016; Godfrey et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2015; Kang et al., 2018). These provide important mechanistic context for interpreting the current findings. The citations are appropriate and accurately represented.

results.result: Summary claims stating that H3K79me2/3 function as activation marks for thermogenic genes, Dot1l is recruited by Zc3h10 to activate thermogenic genes, Dot1l's methyltransferase activity is required for thermogenic gene expression, and Dot1l ablation impairs thermogenesis through decreased H3K79 methylation and chromatin accessibility.
results.evaluation: Claims C101, C103-C108, C118 are high-level summary statements that integrate findings from multiple experiments throughout the paper. These are well-supported by the comprehensive data presented, including protein-protein interaction studies, functional assays in cells and mice, ChIP-qPCR, ATAC-seq, and RNA-seq. The conclusions are justified by the totality of the evidence.

results.result: GWAS database reveals multiple SNPs of Dot1l associated with waist-hip ratio and body mass index in humans.
results.evaluation: Claim C102 cites GWAS database identifiers (HGVPM1111, HGVPM1114) but does not provide details about the strength of associations, sample sizes, or statistical significance. Without access to these specific GWAS entries or more detailed information, it is difficult to evaluate the robustness of these associations. This claim suggests potential human relevance but requires more detailed validation.

results.result: Zc3h10 binds to Dot1l via the coiled coil domain (aa 501-1000), which has been reported to interact with MLL fusion proteins in leukemia.
results.evaluation: Claims C109-C110 are supported by domain mapping data (C10) and citation to Song et al., 2019 for the MLL fusion protein interaction. The parallel with leukemia is interesting and suggests that this domain may be a general protein-protein interaction interface for Dot1l. The citation to Mier et al., 2017 for coiled coil domain function is appropriate.

results.result: Zc3h10 overexpression cannot rescue decreased thermogenic gene expression in Dot1l-BKO mice, and ATAC-seq shows markedly reduced open chromatin regions at thermogenic gene promoters in Dot1l-BKO mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C111-C113 are supported by in vivo rescue experiments (Figure 4H) and ATAC-seq data (Figure 5A). These provide strong evidence for the epistatic relationship between Dot1l and Zc3h10 and the mechanistic role of chromatin accessibility. The claims are consistent with the overall model.

results.result: Speculative statements about potential mechanisms by which H3K79me2/3 may maintain enhancer/promoter associations and work with other histone modifiers.
results.evaluation: Claims C115 and C117 are explicitly speculative ("It is possible that...", "probably works with...") and are not directly tested in this study. While these are reasonable hypotheses based on the data and prior literature, they represent future directions rather than established findings. The speculation is appropriately qualified in the text.

results.result: Summary claims that Dot1l ablation in Ucp1+ cells leads to decreased thermogenic gene expression, cold intolerance, decreased oxygen consumption, increased adiposity, and insulin insensitivity.
results.evaluation: Claims C119-C120 are high-level summaries of the Dot1l-BKO mouse phenotype, integrating data from Figure 4C-G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C. These summary statements are well-supported by the comprehensive phenotypic characterization. The causal chain from reduced thermogenesis to metabolic dysfunction is plausible but somewhat correlative.

results.result: Abstract summary claim that Dot1l ablation using Ucp1-Cre prevents activation of Ucp1 and other target genes to reduce thermogenic capacity and energy expenditure, promoting adiposity.
results.evaluation: Claim C82 is a high-level summary of the main findings presented in the abstract. This is well-supported by the comprehensive data throughout the manuscript, including gene expression, cold tolerance, oxygen consumption, and body weight measurements in Dot1l-BKO mice. The claim accurately represents the major conclusions of the study.
